problems.title: An absolute-value equality forces zero
problems.question: $|b-a|=b+a$ and $a>0$. What must hold?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: Equal real quantities have equal squares.
steps: Squaring gives $(b-a)^2=(b+a)^2$, hence $4ab=0$. Since $a>0$, $b=0$.
Substituting $b=0$ verifies the original equality $|-a|=a$.

problems.title: Sum integer solutions in an interval
problems.question: Find the sum of integer solutions of $x^3|x^2-4x+3|>0$ in $[-2,7)$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: An absolute value is nonnegative and zero only when its argument is zero.
steps: The product is positive exactly for $x>0$ except $x=1,3$, the roots of $(x-1)(x-3)$.
The permitted integers are $2,4,5,6$, whose sum is 17.

problems.title: An equation defined only for negative inputs
problems.question: Solve $(2|x|^3+x^3)/(|x^3|-x^3)=1/2$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: For $x\ge0$ the denominator is zero; for $x<0$, $|x|^3=|x^3|=-x^3$.
steps: On $x<0$, the quotient is $(-2x^3+x^3)/(-2x^3)=1/2$. Every negative input works.
All nonnegative inputs are excluded by the original denominator.

problems.title: A square split by a segment
problems.question: $K$ is on $BC$ of square $ABCD$. Segment $DK$ divides the square area in ratio $1:5$. Find $KC:BK$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: Triangle $DCK$ has area $s\cdot KC/2$, and at most half the square area.
steps: It must be the smaller piece, of area $s^2/6$. Thus $s\cdot KC/2=s^2/6$, giving $KC=s/3$.
Then $BK=2s/3$, so the ratio is $1:2$.

problems.title: Directed sides in a regular hexagon
problems.question: Find $(AB\cdot BC)/(BC\cdot DE)$ in regular hexagon $ABCDEF$, using vector dot products.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The angle between consecutive directed sides $AB,BC$ is $60^\circ$, while that between $BC,DE$ is $120^\circ$.
Equal side lengths cancel, giving $\cos60^\circ/\cos120^\circ=-1$.

problems.title: A polynomial whose range is every real number
problems.question: $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$ has range $\mathbb R$. With $D=b^2-4ac$, what follows?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: A genuine quadratic has a finite maximum or minimum; a nonconstant linear function has range $\mathbb R$.
steps: Therefore $a=0$ and $b\ne0$. Its discriminant expression is $D=b^2>0$.
problems.note: If a nonzero quadratic coefficient were required, the stated range would be impossible. The printed expression does not impose that extra condition.

problems.title: Inverse proportionality after a two-thirds increase
problems.question: $a,b$ are positive and inversely proportional. If $a$ increases by two-thirds of itself, how does $b$ change?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The new $a$ is $(5/3)a$, so the new $b$ is $(3/5)b$.
The reduction is $2/5=40\%$.

problems.title: Absolute value as a nonnegative variable
problems.question: Find the product of real solutions of $x^2-4|x|-5=0$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: Only $t=5$ is nonnegative. Thus $x=5,-5$, whose product is $-25$.

problems.title: Identify a false midpoint vector identity
problems.question: $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Which printed formula for vector $AD$ is false?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The formula $AD=AB+DB$ uses the reversed segment and is false in a nondegenerate triangle.
The other formulas are valid: $AB+BD$, $AB+DC$, and $(AB+AC)/2$ all equal $AD$.

problems.title: Remove a quarter-size triangle
problems.question: $D,E$ are midpoints of $AB,BC$. Find area $ADEC$ if $[ABC]=12$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: $BDE\sim BAC$ with length scale $1/2$, hence area scale $1/4$.
steps: The small triangle has area $12/4=3$. The quadrilateral is the remainder: $12-3=9$.

problems.title: A square-root function and its inverse
problems.question: Which listed point lies on both $y=\sqrt x$ and its inverse?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: Intersections solve $\sqrt x=x^2$, with $x\ge0$. Squaring gives $x=x^4$, so $x=0$ or $x=1$.
The two intersection points are $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$; only $(1,1)$ is listed.

problems.title: A strict absolute-value inequality
problems.question: Solve $|3x-1|<5$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: $-5<3x-1<5$ gives $-4<3x<6$. Divide by 3.

problems.title: A root impossible for every real parameter
problems.question: Which listed number can never solve $x^2-(a^2+6)x+2a^2+8=0$ for real $a$?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The roots are 2 and $a^2+4\ge4$. Thus 3 is impossible.
The other listed values 2,4,5 occur, with 2 always, 4 at $a=0$, and 5 at $a=\pm1$.

problems.title: Coefficients of an internal division vector
problems.question: $AM:MC=2:3$ and $BM=\alpha BA+\beta BC$ as vectors. Find $\alpha+\beta$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: Subtract $B$ to obtain $BM=(3/5)BA+(2/5)BC$.
The sum of coefficients is 1.

problems.title: A vector of a prescribed length and direction
problems.question: Find a length-10 vector directed opposite to $k=(-4,3)$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The opposite unit vector is $-k/5$. Multiply by 10 to obtain $-2k=(8,-6)$.
Its length is $\sqrt{64+36}=10$.

problems.title: Choose the correct work-rate system
problems.question: Two workers together take 12 days. The first alone does half the job, then the second alone does a third, taking 20 days total. Write the system for their individual full-job times $x,y$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: Individual rates are $1/x,1/y$; time for a fraction $f$ is $f$ times the full-job time.
steps: The joint rate gives $1/x+1/y=1/12$. The sequential tasks require $x/2+y/3=20$.
Thus the first listed system correctly models the situation.

problems.title: Extra workers finish two days early
problems.question: 15 workers plan a job for 12 days. After 4 days, more join and the job finishes 2 days early. How many join?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: Total work is 180 worker-days. The first four days complete 60, leaving 120.
The job now ends on day 10, so six days remain. It needs $120/6=20$ workers, which is 5 more than 15.

problems.title: Separate pipe times exceed joint time
problems.question: One pipe alone takes $a$ hours more, and the other $b$ hours more, than their joint time. Find that joint time.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: Multiply through: $t(2t+a+b)=(t+a)(t+b)=t^2+t(a+b)+ab$.
Thus $t^2=ab$ and positivity gives $t=\sqrt{ab}$.

problems.title: Distinct diagonal lengths of a regular polygon
problems.question: A regular $n$-gon has exactly three distinct diagonal lengths. Which listed $n$ works?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: These increase strictly over this range, so there are $\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$ different lengths.
Setting this to 3 gives $n=8$ or 9. Of $9,6,12,10$, only 9 qualifies.

problems.title: An octagon and its alternate-vertex square
problems.question: The square formed by alternate vertices of a regular octagon has area $S$. Find the octagon area.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: Square area with circumradius $R$ is $2R^2$; regular octagon area is $(8/2)R^2\sin45^\circ$.
steps: The octagon area is $2\sqrt2R^2$. Since $S=2R^2$, its area is $S\sqrt2$.

problems.title: Sum reciprocals from equal products
problems.question: $a+b+c=5$ and $ax=by=cz=7$. Find $1/x+1/y+1/z$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: $1/x=a/7$, and similarly for the other variables.
steps: Add the three identities: $(a+b+c)/7=5/7$.

problems.title: A unique zero of a sum of squares
problems.question: $2x^2+4y^2-4xy-2x+1=0$ has unique solution $(a,b)$. Find $a^2+b^2$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: A sum of nonnegative squares is zero only if both vanish. Thus $y=1/2$ and $x-y=1/2$, giving $x=1$.

problems.title: Integer values of a rational absolute-value function
problems.question: How many integer outputs can $(2|x|-1)/(|x|+1)$ take?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The output ranges from $-1$ at $t=0$ up to but not including 2. Every intermediate value is attained.
The integers in $[-1,2)$ are $-1,0,1$.

problems.title: Area ratio for two altitude feet
problems.question: $C=45^\circ$, and $AM,BN$ are altitudes of triangle $ABC$. If $[MNC]=1$, find $[ABC]$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The two triangles share angle $C$. Their area ratio is $(CM\cdot CN)/(CA\cdot CB)=\cos^2C=1/2$.
Thus $[ABC]=2[MNC]=2$.

problems.title: Maximum area for given diagonals
problems.question: What is the greatest area of a quadrilateral with diagonal lengths $m,n$?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: $S=mn|\sin\theta|/2$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the diagonals.
steps: Since $|\sin\theta|\le1$, the area is at most $mn/2$.
Perpendicular diagonals attain this bound, for example in a rhombus with those diagonals.

problems.title: A square whose diagonal directions follow the axes
problems.question: Two square vertices lie on $y=1/x$ in the first quadrant, and the others lie on the two coordinate axes. Diagonals are parallel to the axes. Find area.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: An axis-diagonal square can be written with centre $(h,k)$ and equal diagonal half-length $d$.
steps: The axis vertices must be $(0,k)$ and $(h,0)$, so $h=k=d>0$. The other vertices are $(2d,d)$ and $(d,2d)$.
Both satisfy $xy=1$, giving $2d^2=1$. The diagonals have length $2d$, so area is $(2d)^2/2=2d^2=1$.

problems.title: Length of a radical solution interval
problems.question: Find the length of the solution set of $\sqrt{x+2}\ge x$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: Domain $x\ge-2$; squaring is equivalent only when $x\ge0$.
steps: For $-2\le x<0$, the nonnegative radical is automatically greater than $x$. For $x\ge0$, square to get $x+2\ge x^2$, or $(x-2)(x+1)\le0$.
Combining gives $[-2,2]$, of length 4.

problems.title: Equivalent equations can both have no solutions
problems.question: For how many real $a$ are $|x|=a$ and $\sqrt x=a$ equivalent?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: Equivalent equations have identical real solution sets, including an empty set.
steps: For every $a<0$, neither equation has a real solution, so they are equivalent. At $a=0$, both have the single solution 0.
For $a>0$, the first has two distinct roots $\pm a$, while the second has the single root $a^2$. They cannot be equivalent.

problems.title: Regular dodecagon in a unit circle
problems.question: Find the area of a regular 12-gon inscribed in a circle of radius 1.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: $S=6\sin30^\circ=3$. This is the sum of twelve centre triangles, each of area $1/4$.

problems.title: Remove two quarter-disks from a square
problems.question: Externally touching circles have centres $A,B$ and radii 10,8. Find the area inside square $ABCD$ but outside the circles.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: $AB=10+8=18$; each circle occupies a quarter-disk at its square vertex.
steps: The square area is $18^2=324$. Each circle’s radius is smaller than the side, so its portion inside the square is exactly a quarter-disk.
The two portions do not overlap. Remove $\pi(10^2+8^2)/4=41\pi$.

problems.title: Still-water and current speeds
problems.question: A boat travels 288 km downstream in 8 hours and upstream in 9 hours. Find its still-water speed and the current speed.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The downstream speed is 36 and upstream speed 32 km/h.
Adding and subtracting gives $v=34$ and $c=2$.
problems.answer: Still-water speed 34 km/h; current speed 2 km/h.

problems.title: A median reveals a right triangle
problems.question: Two sides are 10,24, and the median to the third side is 13. Find the area.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: $10^2+24^2=26^2$, hence the triangle is right and its area is $10\cdot24/2=120$.

problems.title: Short base of a right trapezoid
problems.question: $BC,AD$ are the bases of a right trapezoid, $BCD=150^\circ$, and $AC=CD=20$. Find the shorter base.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: The sloping leg makes $30^\circ$ with the base; Pythagoras.
steps: The height is $20\sin30^\circ=10$. In the right triangle with diagonal $AC$, the horizontal leg is $BC$.
Thus $BC=\sqrt{20^2-10^2}=10\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Distance from a square vertex to a segment
problems.question: A unit square has $E$ the midpoint of $AD$. Find the perpendicular distance from $C$ to $BE$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The distance is $|1+2-1|/\sqrt5=2/\sqrt5$. The foot is $(3/5,1/5)$, which lies on segment $BE$.

problems.title: Keep a perimeter unchanged
problems.question: Triangle sides have ratio $2:3:4$. The two smaller sides increase by 10% each. By what percentage should the largest decrease to preserve the perimeter?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: Total increase must equal total decrease.
steps: Write the sides $2k,3k,4k$. The increase is $0.1(2k+3k)=0.5k$.
Relative to the largest side, the required reduction is $0.5k/(4k)=1/8=12.5\%$.

problems.title: Area ratio of two circular segments
problems.question: A chord equal to the circle radius cuts off a smaller segment of area $S$. Find the larger segment area.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The chord condition gives $\theta=\pi/3$. Thus the smaller area is $R^2(\pi/6-\sqrt3/4)=R^2(2\pi-3\sqrt3)/12$.
The larger area is $\pi R^2-S=R^2(10\pi+3\sqrt3)/12$. Divide the two formulas.

problems.title: Do not replace an absolute value by its argument
problems.question: Solve $x\sqrt{x+5}+\sqrt{x^2(x+5)}=0$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The equation is $(x+|x|)\sqrt{x+5}=0$.
Every $x\in[-5,0]$ works, since $x+|x|=0$. For $x>0$, both factors are positive, so there are no further solutions.

problems.title: Recover a quadratic from its tangent minimum
problems.question: $f(x)=2x^2+bx+c$ meets $y=-3$ only at $(1,-3)$. Solve $f(x)=x$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: The unique horizontal intersection is the vertex, so $f(x)=2(x-1)^2-3$.
steps: Expanding gives $f(x)=2x^2-4x-1$. Set equal to $x$: $2x^2-5x-1=0$.
The quadratic formula gives $(5\pm\sqrt{25+8})/4$.

problems.title: Recover all three triangle sides
problems.question: A triangle has area $15\sqrt3$, $A=120^\circ$, and circumradius $14/\sqrt3$. Find its sides.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
steps: The opposite side is $a=2(14/\sqrt3)(\sqrt3/2)=14$. The area formula gives $bc=60$.
The cosine rule gives $196=b^2+c^2+60$, so $b^2+c^2=136$. Then $(b+c)^2=256$, hence $b+c=16$.
The numbers $b,c$ are roots of $t^2-16t+60=0$, namely 6 and 10. They satisfy the triangle inequality with 14.

problems.title: Maximize a sector with a fixed amount of fencing
problems.question: A farmer has $100\text{ m}^2$ of fencing material. Along the two radii the fence is 1 m high, and along the sector arc it is 2 m high. Find the greatest enclosed area and central angle.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into a formula and solve it with all restrictions retained.
formulas: Fencing constraint $2r+2r\theta=100$; sector area $A=r^2\theta/2$, with radians.
steps: Eliminate the angle: $\theta=50/r-1$. Thus $A=25r-r^2/2=625/2-(r-25)^2/2$.
The squared term is nonnegative, so $A\le625/2$, attained at $r=25$. At that radius $\theta=1$ radian, a valid sector angle.
The arc length is 25, using 50 square metres of fence; the two radii also use 50. The whole budget is used, so equality is attainable.
problems.answer: Maximum $312.5\text{ m}^2$, with radius 25 m and central angle 1 radian.
